title: Sonata for Trumpet and Piano
program_note:
This Sonata was inspired, in part, by Brahms’ Clarinet Sonata No.1, in its flexible approach to the by-then-standard overall sonata form.  The first movement is loosely sonata form in structure, with a repeating-note introduction.  The second movement is a nostalgic recollection of a rainy Paris street.  The last movement, fittingly, is a rondo, but a rondo that creates an intricate fugue.
It is written in a variety of newly-created “modes” (or scales):  the first movement is based on a repeating major-second/major-second/minor-third interval pattern; the second movement is based on a lydian tetrachord repeated at the perfect fifth; and counteracting the relative openness of the first previous movement, the last movement is based on the same lydian tetrachord with the first step filled in.  In each case, the resulting scale changes color as it gets higher or lower.

The music is about 19’30” in duration, as follows:

1.  9’40”
2.  3’45”
iii. 6’00”

David S. Lef kowitz
Los Angeles, CA
25 April, 2023
